item.title: ‘I’ll keep fighting until the day I die’: data centres ignite revolt in Japan
item.description: Until a ⁠few years ago, Susumu Goto’s house in Kashiwa, northeast of Tokyo, looked out on a grassy field where neighbours played baseball and soccer. Today, a couple of 31-metre-tall (102-foot) data centres owned by Hong Kong-based asset manager PAG loom in front of it. At least once a month, tests of backup generators send black fumes into the sky and the smell of burning fuel hangs in the air. “Every morning when I step outside, my whole view is swallowed up by the buildings,” said the retired... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
